title: Recommendation strength (GRADE, as WHO applies it)
description: The strength of a recommendation in a guideline developed with the GRADE approach, as the WHO handbook for guideline development applies it: how confident the guideline group is that the desirable effects of following the recommendation outweigh the undesirable ones. Named by a `recommendation` block's `strength` (bean 55ao).

source.note: WHO handbook for guideline development, 2nd edition (2014); ingested in the WHO IRIS library as `9789241548960-eng`. Owner ruling 2026-09-23 (bean 55ao, Q2): strength names a concept in a declared scheme, and each domain brings its own.

codes.label: Strong recommendation
codes.definition: The guideline group is confident that the desirable effects of adherence outweigh the undesirable effects; most people in the situation would want the recommended course of action.

codes.label: Conditional recommendation
codes.definition: The guideline group concludes that the desirable effects of adherence probably outweigh the undesirable effects, but is less confident; the choice depends on values, preferences and setting. Earlier editions called this a weak recommendation.
